runs.t: By the end of class, you can do these six things.
I can ask Whose… is this?
I can say mine, yours, hers, or Ana's.
I can ask Is this yours? → Yes, it's mine.
I can describe a lost item.
I can say what I was doing when I lost it.
I can read and write a FOUND notice.

slides.notes:
Read each goal slowly. Learners repeat.
Goal 1: Whose… is this? / Whose… are these? Goal 2: mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs or a name + 's (It's Ana's.). Goal 3: Is this yours? → Yes, it's mine. / No, it isn't mine.
Goal 4: size, color, and details (a small black wallet with a zipper). Goal 5: I was waiting for the bus when I lost it. Goal 6: read a FOUND notice, fill out a lost-item report, and write a short FOUND notice.
"We check at 7:25" = the Progress Check. It is not a test grade.

Listening script (the audio is coming soon; until then, read it aloud with a volunteer at a normal, friendly speed):
Narrator: Lesson eight. Listening. David lost something on the bus. He's calling the lost and found. Listen.
Joan: City Bus, Lost and Found. How can I help you?
David: Hi. I lost my backpack on the bus this morning.
Joan: OK. Can you describe it?
David: It's a big blue backpack with a black zipper. My brother has the same one, but his is green.
Joan: What was inside?
David: My headphones, a red scarf, and some gloves.
Joan: And what were you doing when you lost it?
David: I was talking on the phone. I got off at Park Street, and I left it on the seat.
Joan: Let me check. We have two blue backpacks. One is small, and one is big.
David: The big one is mine.
Joan: There are white headphones inside. Are they yours?
David: No, mine are black. Those aren't mine.
Joan: Wait. Here's another big one, with black headphones and a red scarf.
David: Yes! That's mine. Thank you!
Joan: You're welcome. You can pick it up today before five.
Narrator: That's the end of the listening.

Then: "Whose and who's sound the same: hooz." Read the line in the "Say it" box (Whose bag is this?). The class repeats each line twice.

Step 6 · 7:12–7:17 · Exit Ticket + Homework · 5 min · NEVER SKIP.
Exit ticket: each learner writes two sentences on a slip: one with a possessive pronoun (This umbrella isn't mine. It's hers.), and one about losing something with when and because or so (I was waiting for the bus when I lost my keys, so I called the lost and found.). Collect at the door.

slides.title: Before You Go

runs.t: I can ask Whose… is this?
I can say It's mine / It's hers.
I can describe a lost item.
I can fill out a lost-item report.
A. Listen to the teacher. Circle a or b.
a. They're the speaker's keys.   b. They're someone else's keys.
a. It's his umbrella.   b. It's her umbrella.
a. a small black wallet   b. a big brown wallet
a. The gloves are ours.   b. The gloves are theirs.

slides.notes:
Progress Check · 7:25–7:30 · 5 min. Individuals. Open the Progress Check page.
Part A: read each sentence slowly, 2 times. Learners circle a or b. Then click to show the answer (one click per item, 1 to 4).
Say: 1 "Whose keys are these? They're mine." (a) • 2 "Is this your umbrella? No, it's hers." (b) • 3 "I lost a small black wallet." (a) • 4 "These gloves aren't ours. They're theirs." (b)
Parts B and C: learners do them alone. Walk around and help with the instructions only. B answers: 1 Whose, 2 mine, 3 Their, 4 yours. C: answers will vary (for example I lost a big red backpack with a zipper. / It's mine. / It's Ana's.).
Part D: read each "I can…" line aloud and point to the 3 faces: 😀 "I can do it." 🙂 "With a little help." 😐 "Not yet."
Scoring: A /4 + B /4 + C /2 = /10. This is not a test grade. It shows who needs more help hearing possessives (A) and with the forms (B, C).
Collect the pages (or check them at the start of Week 10). If behind: do the Progress Check in Week 10 at 6:00, while learners arrive.
